content.text: The text combines excerpts from several historical works: John Evelyn’s diary (1689–1705), describing political upheaval, religious disputes, wars, weather, scientific and cultural life, family deaths, and the founding of Greenwich Hospital; memoirs of Minnesota’s territorial printers, Civil War service, and St. Paul society; accounts of the battles of Mill Springs and Pittsburg Landing; a young woman’s diaries recording family, weddings, travel, religious life, and her grandmother’s death; and essays comparing Maya, Egyptian, African, Asian, and American cultures, especially writing, mythology, customs, and music. It also includes advertisements, market reports, bibliographical notices, and editorial corrections. Notable movements include Evelyn’s visits to London, Lambeth, Wotton, Deptford, Kensington, Eton, and Greenwich; the diarist’s travels through England, Scotland, Paris, and America; and soldiers’ movements through Kentucky, Tennessee, Mississippi, and the Dakotas.
